newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sees higher 1997 tourism revenue.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sees higher 1997 tourism revenue.

text.p: Croatia expects its total revenues from tourism in 1997 to reach between 12 and 13 billion kuna, or 20 percent up from projections for this year, the tourism ministry said on Tuesday.

Assistant Tourism Minister Marijan Bulat said the 1996 season was the most successful since Croatia won independence from former Yugoslavia in 1991, which led to conflict with rebel minority Serbs ending in 1995.

Some 20.5 million overnight bookings were recorded in the first nine months of 1996, almost 70 percent up on the previous year, with total revenues expected to reach between 9 and 10 billion kuna by the end of the year.

Bulat gave an equally optimistic estimate for 1997, putting the figure of expected overnights at 26.5 million kuna, and total revenues between 12 and 13 billion kuna. ($1 = 5.4301 kuna) -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4551-840
